title: Engaging Teachers to Co-Design Integrated AI Curriculum for K-12 Classrooms
extended_summary:
This paper asks how AI education can be made more accessible and how AI concepts can be integrated into core K-12 subjects. The authors note that much prior AI education work is standalone, often teacher-uninvolved, and not designed for diverse classroom contexts. They therefore focus on teacher values, needs, and practical considerations for integrating AI into non-computing curricula.

The intervention was a two-day remote co-design workshop with 15 K-12 educators. Participants first learned basic AI concepts and explored AI tools, then worked in small groups to co-create lesson plans that embedded AI into social studies, ESL, and literacy for students with learning disabilities. The workshop included pre-work, group design sessions, an ethics/diversity presentation, and researcher facilitation. Data came from workshop audio, questionnaires, and participant deliverables, analyzed thematically.

The study found that teachers emphasized evaluation, engagement, logistics, and collaboration when designing AI-integrated lessons. The resulting curricula used data, reflection, and ethics as main integration points. The authors conclude that AI can be embedded into core subjects to broaden access beyond CS classrooms, but that teacher scaffolding, curriculum supports, and contextual adaptation are essential for classroom implementation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative co-design and reflection paper, not a causal comparison study. It does not test an intervention on student outcomes, and it reports no experimental design, delayed post-tests, or transfer tasks.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has practical relevance for curriculum design and teacher adoption, especially for integrated AI instruction in non-CS subjects and for diverse learners, but it provides no measurable student impact. Its contribution is conceptual and implementation-oriented rather than evidence of learning gains.

interventions.use_case: remote co-design workshop for K-12 teachers to design integrated AI curriculum materials using AI learning tools and exemplars
